- [FACT] The user is interested in the role of the Khalifa in the Ahmadiyya community and its relation to the teachings of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Khalifa in the Ahmadiyya community functions as the spiritual leader and guide, considered the successor of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Khalifa is responsible for interpreting the teachings of Ahmad and applying them to modern-day circumstances.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Khalifa guides the community in matters of faith, provides religious education, and oversees community projects and initiatives.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mirza Ghulam Ahmad's teachings emphasized following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, promoting peace and tolerance, and spiritual and moral development.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Khalifa is expected to maintain a high moral standard and the Ahmadiyya community emphasizes obedience to the Khalifa.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The selection of a Khalifa occurs within a few days of the previous Khalifa's death, starting with community condolences.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Senior members of the community gather to select the new Khalifa after praying for guidance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The council considers the candidate's personal qualities, knowledge of the faith, and leadership experience.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Once a candidate is selected and accepts the responsibility, he is officially announced as the new Khalifa.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The succession of Khalifas is seen as a divine process ensuring the community's guidance and growth.
- [USER] The user finds the selection process of Khalifas interesting.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community has had 5 Khalifas so far.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The list of Khalifas includes:
  1. Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad - 2003 to present
  2. Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad - 1982 to 2003
  3. Hazrat Mirza Nasir Ahmad - 1965 to 1982
  4. Hazrat Mirza Bashiruddin Mahmood Ahmad - 1914 to 1965
  5. Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad - 1889 to 1908
